title: Conversational handshake: stream event surface and adaptive retry ergonomics for Python SDK
creator: Priya Reddy
description:
Problem: Customers building interactive chat UIs keep asking for a small, well-documented set of streaming primitives that make it easy to implement deterministic reconnection, prefix resumption, and low-latency incremental rendering while preserving idempotency and giving clear telemetry. Existing py-sdk ergonomics are powerful but have inconsistent signal names and limited guidance for adaptive retries and backpressure handling.

Goal: Ship a compact, idiomatic Python streaming surface (the 'conversational handshake') that: (1) exposes a typed event callback/iterator set for handshake/open/checkpoint/event/error/close; (2) provides helper primitives for adaptive client-side retries (with idempotency token guidance) and graceful backpressure; (3) emits structured telemetry hooks suitable for Console tracing and cost breakdown; (4) includes cookbook examples and a migration guide.

Non-goals: Provide a full stateful session manager (we will provide lightweight helpers and recipes only). Do not change wire protocol or server event shapes.

Proposal summary: Introduce ChatStreamHandshake, a tiny surface atop the existing streaming client that exposes: - on_handshake(metadata) - on_delta(delta, seq) - on_checkpoint(checkpoint_id, resume_token) - on_signal(signal_type) - on_error(err, retryable) - on_close(final_status)
Each callback receives a typed event object (simple dataclass) with stable attributes (token, seq, latency_ms, source_model, truncated). The primary consumer API will be an async iterator wrapper with context-manager semantics:

  async with ChatStreamHandshake(client.create_stream(req)) as stream:
      async for evt in stream.events():
          if isinstance(evt, HandshakeEvent): ...
          elif isinstance(evt, DeltaEvent): render_incrementally(evt.text)

Helpers: - RetryPolicy.adaptive(backoff_base_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=2000, jitter=True) which consults event signals and checkpoint age to decide soft vs hard retry. - idempotency_token_from_prompt(prompt, metadata) helper to compute stable token recommendations. - backpressure_coordinator(max_queue=128, drop_strategy="tail") for bounded consumer buffers.

Telemetry: Add three lightweight hooks: on_stream_open(metrics), on_stream_event(metrics), on_stream_close(metrics). These emit flat key/value maps suitable for Redwood Console ingestion. We will log token counts, cumulative latency, and whether a resume occurred.

Compatibility & rollout: Feature flag in client (enable_handshake=True). Default off for 1 release to collect opt-in feedback. Full docs and cookbook to be published in SDK docs.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: Developers may misuse idempotency token causing duplicates. Mitigation: provide explicit doc + unit tests + lint rule example. - Risk: surface complexity. Mitigation: keep high-level iterator as primary API and callbacks as opt-in advanced mode.
acceptance_criteria: ChatStreamHandshake exists in the py-sdk public module and is behind enable_handshake feature flag
Async iterator usage documented with two cookbook examples (reconnect/resume and adaptive retry) published in SDK docs
RetryPolicy.adaptive implemented with deterministic unit tests covering jitter/backoff bounds and checkpoint age decisions
Telemetry hooks emit the three expected metric groups and have Console wiring (events show up in dev Console when opt-in)
Performance: default iterator adds <1ms median overhead to existing streaming client in microbenchmarks
Integration test: simulate interrupted stream and verify resume_token usage restores correct prefix state
